The river crested at midnight. By morning, the downtown was under four feet of water. Sandbags had failed. The levee held, barely. National Guard units arrived by helicopter. They found families on rooftops. They found dogs swimming in parking lots. The shelter at the high school filled within hours. Cots ran out. Food ran low. A local bakery donated everything it had. A hardware store gave away every pump in stock. That is what happens in floods. Strangers become neighbors. Neighbors become heroes. The damage estimate hit fifty million dollars by the end of the week. Insurance will cover a fraction of it. Federal aid will take months. Some homes will never be rebuilt. The mayor stood in mud up to her ankles and promised the town would recover. She meant it. But recovery is a long word. It takes years to live up to.
